transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-15 | Start: 17:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Location: All-hands (Zoom)
Attendees: Maya Singh, Tom Alvarez, Priya Patel, Ben Carter, Sofia Ramos, Liam O'Connor + All Staff

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the spring all-hands. I know it's, uh, a busy week, so appreciate the time. Quick agenda — finance/hiring, product updates, ops and reliability, then Q&A. We'll try to keep it tight.

[00:18] Tom: Quick note on audio, I might drop in and out, internet acting up.

[00:25] Maya: ok, first up Liam on numbers. Liam?

[00:28] Liam: yeah hi all. Quick pack — Q1 performance came in slightly better than the internal plan, revenue growth around 18% quarter over quarter, pipeline healthy but conversion is slower in enterprise segment, our burn rate lowered by about 8% after the infra cost optimization. Runway sits at about 10.5 months under current plan. We are recommending a small hiring pause for non-critical IC roles to prioritize key hires in infra and product.

[00:56] Maya: clarifying, pause for non-critical means contractor conversion and generic marketing ICs can wait; frontline eng and se hiring continues. Correct?

[01:05] Liam: yes that's the plan.

[01:08] Sofia: On hiring — we'll rescope onboarding for remote hires, centralize interview rubrics. Expect the list by Monday. Also note we're launching a flexible leave policy pilot in June, details in Slack hr-channel.

[01:26] Maya: great, thanks. Priya, product update.

[01:30] Priya: Hi — long version: three product streams: Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private plus Redwood Optimize features. Quick hits: Dedicated GA scheduling looks on track for late Q3, Private VPC beta has 6 customers in trial, and Optimize small feature set (caching and batching suggestions) is shipping as an opt-in early access next week. We're also aligning the rollout with the console observability changes so customers see cost/latency tradeoffs in situ.

[02:05] Ben: quick interjection — can we call out the KV cache improvements? The latency reduction is material for small-context chat workloads.

[02:12] Priya: yes, KV cache + smarter batching; engineering knocked down median p50 latency by ~12% in internal perf tests w/ current quantization profile. Note: results vary by model and sequence length.

[02:28] Maya: good. On the Dedicated timeline — what's runway risk if Dedicated sells slower than expected?

[02:35] Liam: we modeled two scenarios — base and conservative. Even in conservative where Dedicated revenue lags by two quarters, runway stays >9 months with the hiring pause and some discretionary spend cut. Still, we want to accelerate trial conversions. Sales, please coordinate with product marketing.

[02:50] Sofia: one people question — what about hiring managers' ability to interview? We need to streamline to avoid long cycles.

[02:56] Maya: agreed, more structure. Ben, ops and reliability overview?

[03:00] Ben: Yep. Quick recap of April 18 outage — root cause was an autoscaling edge case plus a kernel scheduler regression on a specific GPU driver version. We rolled back, mitigations applied, and improved autoscaler safety checks. We're adding an automated canary for kernel/driver changes and improving tracing to catch the cold-start regression earlier.

[03:28] Ben: SLA compliance remains high, but we had a few customers impacted. We're offering credits and a follow-up executive outreach. Internally, postmortem will be published and shared; Priya will link it to the roadmap so folks see how reliability work maps to product prioritization.

[03:45] Maya: good, thank you. Security/compliance? Tom?

[03:48] Tom: Security is on track — SOC 2 Type II audit is scheduled for late June. We've closed 14 of the 18 outstanding remediation items from the readiness run; remaining items are around logging retention and improved KMS key rotation automation. Private customers asked about HSM options — engineering is prototyping a KMS/HSM integration path for the private stack. Note: some terminology in the SR docs is fuzzy — the audit team will tidy the language.

[04:20] Audience question (Slack): What about data residency for EU customers?

[04:24] Tom: working on multi-region control plane options and are planning a EU-only private region for regulated customers; timeline depends on partner infra procurement but targeted for Q4.

[04:40] Maya: recognition — shout out to infra team for the swift rollback and to SEs who ran customer comms — appreciate that. Also four people completed promotions this cycle, congratulations to: Aisha Rahman (Staff SW Eng), Jorge Mendez (Senior SE), Hannah Lee (SWE II), and Marcus Huang (Product Designer).

[05:05] Sofia: ppl update — compensation review window opens next week, and managers please prepare calibration notes. Also a reminder about parental leave policy update pilot starting June 1.

[05:18] Live Q&A

[05:20] Employee (Austin): Hi, question on pricing — will we update hosted API pricing to reflect caching gains? Some customers asking for token-based discounts when cache hit rates are high.

[05:30] Maya: good question. Pricing changes are tricky. We're evaluating pricing experiments that factor in effective token counts after caching; Liam and product finance will present options to execs next week.

[05:40] Liam: the sensitivity analysis will show how unit economics change with caching and batching; one option is to introduce a credit for cached responses under certain SLAs.

[05:48] Employee (Rae): Any update on support SLAs for Dedicated customers?

[05:52] Ben: Dedicated will have a higher SLA tier with a dedicated support channel and faster incident response times; final SLA numbers are being defined with sales. Expect a doc in the sales playbook.

[06:05] Employee (Jordan): Will Private support air-gapped / on-prem deployments for regulated banks?

[06:10] Tom: yes, the on-prem package supports air-gapped installs; we are evaluating automation for updates that don't require internet egress. HSM/KMS options are in scope. There's a cost tradeoff — we'll document that for customers.

[06:24] Employee (M): Roadmap question — are we reprioritizing features for model-ops (e.g., easy quantization and kernel selection tooling)?

[06:30] Priya: yes model-ops is a priority for next two quarters — we want to provide better first-party quantization profiles and a small set of cli tools to help customers onboard models faster. We'll add a short alpha program for select partners.

[06:46] Cross talk / laughter / brief static on call

[06:52] Maya: Ok, a couple of tactical asks before we close. Priya — share updated roadmap deck w/ feature-level timelines. Ben — publish postmortem. Sofia — hiring priorities & rubrics. Liam — runway sensitivity. We'll reconvene for a 30-min follow-up town hall in late June to review SOC2 outcomes.

[07:20] Ben: quick note — engineering will have an all-hands next week focused on infra reliability deep-dive, attendance expected for infra and SRE adjacent teams.

[07:30] Maya: thanks everyone. We'll bring the recording and notes into the #all-hands channel and the Confluence page. End of meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: Speaker attributions automated; some names may be mis-attributed. There are brief audio drops and overlap crosstalk around Q&A timestamps.
